law.what: One pinned upper bound per program per kernel envelope, priced in the kernel's own verifier cost: the verified_insns count the kernel reports for the loaded program (UAPI aba64c7da983, 2021-10-21 - bpf: Add verified_insns to bpf_prog_info and fdinfo), read live by the census in scripts/supermassive/verifier-budget-test.py through the kernel's own channels (the bpf() syscall for the program walk and the name, the program fd's /proc fdinfo for the price). The objects are byte-identical by construction (the parity gates), so for one kernel the number is deterministic - the budget pins the verifier walk, not a sample of it.
law.growth_law: A measured value above the pinned budget fails the battery. Raising a budget requires the commit that raises it to name the new number and the reason in the row's history (a raise is never silent - the growth is the event the gate exists to name).
law.ratchet_law: A budget may be lowered any time; the history records the lower value; a measured value below the budget never fails - it prints the headroom, and the ratchet (lowering the pin to the measured number) is the encouraged follow-up.
law.completeness_law: Every program the estate loads carries a row in BOTH envelopes. A loaded program missing from the ledger fails the battery on every run, census mode included - the inventory gate arms at landing and is never deferred; only the budget comparison defers.
law.census_law: A null budget is census debt, named honestly: the battery measures the program, prints the number into the run log (MASS-CENSUS rows), and the budget comparison stays deferred while armed is false. The arming commit pins the measured numbers from a watched CI run and flips armed to true in the same change - no half-armed state exists (armed true with any null budget is an invalid ledger).
law.availability_law: The verified_insns field landed in the v5.16 merge window - the 5.15 floor kernel does not expose it, and no honest pin can exist there. The floor envelope is therefore an inventory envelope: its rows stay null forever (a pinned budget there would be fabrication), its gate is the load-proof itself (every estate program seen = the objects still load on the floor kernel). The head envelope prices by verified_insns.

floor.kernel_class: uname -r 5.15.* - the jammy 5.15.0-ABI line, the documented 5.15.0 floor contract (verified_insns does not exist on it: the UAPI field landed in the v5.16 merge window)

head.kernel_class: uname -r not 5.15.* - the archive's latest kernel, resolved dynamically at run time (any kernel at or past v5.16 exposes the field)
